extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers, screenwriters, and creative-writing students
extracted.subtask_description: Formulating a one-sentence 'controlling idea' (premise/moral/theme statement) that states the value change caused within a story and that is embodied by plot and dramatized by the climax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Controlling Idea
rubrics_metrics.description: A single sentence that captures how and why life undergoes change from one condition at the beginning to another at the end of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the same concept as Egri's 'premise', McKee's 'controlling idea', theology's 'moral premise', or a screenwriting 'theme statement'. It should explain the story-specific causal claim about value change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form: [Value Charge] + [Cause]
rubrics_metrics.description: Controlling idea should take the form: [Value Charge] + [Cause] (e.g., 'Justice prevails because…').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value charge indicates positive/negative charge (redemption, tragedy, transformation). Examples: 'Justice prevails because…' (positive); 'Love is destroyed by…' (negative); 'Wisdom emerges through…' (transformation).

rubrics_metrics.name: How to discover it (McKee method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Look at your climactic action and ask: 'As a result of this climactic action, what value, positively or negatively charged, is brought into the world of my protagonist?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start from the climax's outcome and work backward to state the causal value-change claim that the climax dramatizes. The climax is the test and reveal of the controlling idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Criterion: States the story's value charge
rubrics_metrics.description: The controlling idea must state the story's value charge (positive or negative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly indicate whether the story affirms or denies a value (e.g., 'good triumphs' vs. 'pride destroys'). The charge anchors the emotional/ethical direction of the tale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Criterion: Specifies the cause
rubrics_metrics.description: The controlling idea must specify the cause — what produces the stated value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the causal mechanism or human action that leads to the value change (e.g., 'through sacrifice', 'because ambition corrupts'). This links plot action to thematic outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Criterion: Fits in one sentence
rubrics_metrics.description: The controlling idea should fit in a single sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brevity forces precision: the single-sentence form helps ensure the premise is a clear, testable causal claim rather than a vague observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Criterion: Is embodied in plot, not announced
rubrics_metrics.description: The controlling idea must be embodied in the plot rather than being explicitly announced to the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid telling or lecturing the theme; show it through events and character choices. Anti-pattern: characters stating the moral outright without the plot demonstrating it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Criterion: Tested by climactic action
rubrics_metrics.description: The controlling idea should be tested and dramatized by the climactic action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The climax should enact the causal claim so readers/audience can see the controlling idea validated or falsified by what happens at the story's turning point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Criterion: Discoverable in retrospect by readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers should be able to discover the controlling idea in retrospect after seeing the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The idea must be evident when the reader reviews the arc; it should not be so obscure that retrospective sense-making is impossible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Test: Can you state it in one sentence?
rubrics_metrics.description: A practical test — see if you can state your story's controlling idea in one sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot, the idea is likely unfocused or too diffuse. Use this as an editing checkpoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Test: Does the climax dramatize that idea?
rubrics_metrics.description: Check whether the climax explicitly dramatizes the controlling idea's causal claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the climax doesn't put the claimed value/cause to the test, the controlling idea is not effectively realized and should be revised or the plot adjusted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Test: Does each major scene engage the value at stake?
rubrics_metrics.description: Each major scene should engage, challenge, or illuminate the value central to the controlling idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scenes should repeatedly confront the protagonist with choices or situations that make the value visible; otherwise the story may feel episodic or aimless.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Test: Would the theme be embodied differently and lose meaning?
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether the theme is specific to this embodiment — could the idea be embodied differently and thereby lose its meaning?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This test checks whether the controlling idea is tightly bound to plot and character choices rather than being a generic slogan. If the theme survives any embodiment unchanged, it may be too vague or abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish Controlling Idea vs Moral vs Theme
rubrics_metrics.description: Moral = a specific lesson; Theme = a larger concept emerging from patterns; Controlling Idea = the precise causal claim about value change in this story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this distinction to ensure your statement is the story-specific causal claim (controlling idea) rather than a general proverb (moral) or a broad subject (theme).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples as exemplars
rubrics_metrics.description: Model controlling ideas from well-known works (e.g., 'Tyranny self-destructs through the very ambition that sustains it' — Macbeth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete examples to see how value+cause is phrased and embodied by plot and climax; compare your phrasing to these exemplars to judge clarity and specificity.
